.engramdb/memories/staging-export-bucket-points-at-the-prod-bucket_01a0f904-94a3-7141-a811-e6ac23cff7c2.md:15:In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Never run scripts/export.py against staging without `--dry-run`.

Yes, but only with `--dry-run`.

In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. A real run against staging would write to prod. This comes from a stored project memory, not from the script. `scripts/export.py` reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` from the environment and only falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev` when it's unset.

The script does support the flag. It has `--dry-run` at `scripts/export.py:8`, and it prints the target bucket and the `dry_run` value at line 11.

```
python scripts/export.py <env> --dry-run
```

I haven't run it. I only read the script, and I haven't checked what the `<env>` argument expects. Run it with `--dry-run` first and confirm the printed line shows `dry_run=True`. Be aware that I can't tell from the code whether `--dry-run` actually skips the upload. This grep only showed it being parsed and printed. If you want to test a real export, point `EXPORT_BUCKET` at a dev or scratch bucket first.

If you want, I can read the rest of `scripts/export.py` to confirm `--dry-run` blocks all writes.
